tags.gist: Calls the paper among FDA's most thoughtful on GenAI, well aligned with a lifecycle approach, while offering additional inputs from cloud platform work.
Wants explicit multiple-function product examples, boundary controls and evidence of independence where one foundation model serves regulated and non-regulated functions.
Wants a dedicated cybersecurity competency area, or alignment with FDA cybersecurity guidance and standards, covering poisoning, retrieval attacks and tool abuse.
Wants human factors validation, including trust calibration, overreliance, alert fatigue and automation bias, as a standalone evaluation pillar.
Says most systems use retrieval, and wants validation expectations defined separately for the foundation model, retrieval layer, orchestrator and final output.
Finds the statistics vague and suggests non-inferiority or Bayesian approaches, risk-adjusted thresholds and team effectiveness measures.
Thinks agentic risk is understated and wants approval checkpoints, tool-use verification, audit trails, rollback and runtime supervision before high-risk deployment.
Calls provider-initiated model changes the biggest practical challenge and wants locked versions, traceability, supplier agreements, triggered revalidation and PCCP provisions.
